summary: Slow query against large issues table with complex authorization predicates, EXISTS subquery, NOT IN subquery, leading-wildcard LIKE on subject, and ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 10.
symptoms: EXPLAIN shows issues scanned with PRIMARY key range and Using where
Dependent subqueries evaluated per-row for enabled_modules and members
mechanism: Non-sargable text filter (LOWER(subject) LIKE '%...%') prevents index use and forces scanning many issues in descending PK order to find 10 matches; complex OR predicates and correlated checks add CPU and lookups. In MySQL, the NOT IN members predicate may be executed via a materialized deduplicated list probed per row; data skew and rarity of the searched token near high ids exacerbate the scan length.

facts.evidence: The question text lists table record counts.
The system currently has 1350 users. Currently only goes to 100 concurrent users.

value.select: SELECT issues.* FROM issues INNER JOIN projects ON projects.id = issues.project_id WHERE (...) AND (LOWER(issues.subject) LIKE LOWER('%255392%')) ORDER BY issues.id DESC LIMIT 10

facts.evidence: Full query provided in the post.
Tabular EXPLAIN included in the post.

assumptions: MySQL version is 5.6/5.7/8.0 with InnoDB and default case-insensitive collation for subject; no fulltext indexes on issues.subject.
The searched token ('255392') is rare among the newest issues (high ids), forcing long PK-desc scans to find 10 matches.
Indexes exist on issues(project_id), enabled_modules(project_id,name), and members(user_id, project_id) as suggested by EXPLAIN, but there is no usable index for the LIKE predicate.
OR-heavy authorization predicates and subqueries inhibit use of composite indexes and encourage a PK-ordered scan with filter.
unknowns: Exact MySQL version and optimizer settings (e.g., semijoin/materialization strategies)
Exact data distribution across projects and subjects, and user membership patterns
Presence of any covering/compound indexes in production beyond those shown in EXPLAIN possible_keys
